steps.content: [Manor]
Only when the last whisper of wind finally dies away do you manage to struggle free from the broken tiles. As far as the eye can see, nothing remains but an empty, deathly silence.

You stumble through the rubble. There, half-buried in dust, lies the ornate embroidery of Shen Wanchou's robe. Nearby, you find a pipa, its body shattered beyond recognition, and a walking stick, twisted into a useless shape.
You pass the snow mound where the martial artists were hastily buried. Now, a scattering of crimson petals blankets it in a tender, silent embrace.
Jichuan—
Your voice echoes off the broken walls, then quickly fades away.
Shuang'er—
Still, there is no response.

That final gust of wind has ripped the last of the plum blossoms from the branches. In the ravaged courtyard, the boughs now hold not a single speck of red; the ground below is smothered in a thick carpet of fallen petals.
As you stare up at the naked limbs, a steamed bun sails through the air and smacks you squarely on the head.

steps.speaker: Xiaofeng
steps.content: Stop wailing. You're hurting my ears.
Perched on the eaves next to a ridge beast, Xiaofeng dangles her legs and casually swings a liquor jar, its contents nearly gone.

steps.speaker: Xiaofeng
steps.content: That girl you're looking for... when she sent me down to fetch you, yeah, she did leave a message.

steps.speaker: Xiaofeng
steps.content: Pfft, what was it again? Something about the martial world, the righteous path... real theatrical stuff, like an opera. Anyway, her last words were way too long. Who the **** can remember all that flowery nonsense!
At the sound of "last words," you waver on your feet, nearly losing your balance.
From the eaves above, Xiaofeng suddenly lets out a laugh and leaps down.

steps.speaker: Xiaofeng
steps.content: Lucky for you, you've kept a trick up your sleeve. That red thorn thing you shot out... what even was that? Whatever. Long story short, she's still breathing.
She raises her hand, pointing sharply toward the old plum tree at the cliff's edge.

steps.speaker: Xiaofeng
steps.content: There, see that? Want to hear her finish that line? Go ask her yourself.
[Cliff]

The snow beneath the plum tree lies in rough, cleared heaps, leaving several large tiger paw prints stamped into the frozen earth. Jichuan sits propped against the tree roots, half-reclining, appearing as if asleep.
Jichuan?
She hears your voice and her eyes flutter open. She is alive. Her pupils, shaped like plum blossoms, are unfocused; they catch the light from the sky, yet remain shrouded, as if in a mist.

steps.speaker: Jichuan
steps.content: Is it... dawn? I can't see clearly anymore.

A thousand questions burn on your tongue. You want to ask if every shared day was part of her scheme, if she hesitated for even a single heartbeat before pushing you from that cliff. But when you finally speak, you don't ask a single one. You simply answer her.
It's dawn. The snow stopped.

steps.speaker: Jichuan
steps.content: Liar... I can still hear the wind.
There is no wind, only the faint, barely perceptible whisper of snow on the verge of melting. You know she won't be able to hear much longer.
It's not wind. It's the plum blossoms falling.
She pauses, a moment of stillness passing before a gentle smile touches her lips.

steps.speaker: Jichuan
steps.content: Then... can you listen for me? What other sounds are there?
You pause, the silence settling between you. Then, slowly, word by word, you paint for her a picture of the sights she will never see again.

Snow's melting off the eaves. Drip, drip... really slow, but steady. Birds are calling from the mountain behind us. Not larks, sparrows, chattering away, probably fighting over the last frozen berries on the branches.
And... children laughing down in the valley. It's far away, but they're definitely laughing.

steps.speaker: Jichuan
steps.content: ...Really?

options: Really. They all know your story now.

steps.content: You whisper to her of the town below—their hopes, their dreams, their unbroken faith in heroes. Her wish has come true; she is now the hero she always wanted to be.
Listening, she seizes your hand with excitement, her own ice-cold and light as feathers. You gently part her fingers and lift her palm to the sky.
Can you feel it? The sun's breaking through.

steps.speaker: Jichuan
steps.content: ...Yes. It's warm.

That mountain across from Mount Fuyun... what's it called? The snow's melting there too. There's a stretch of rock showing at the peak. And the cooking smoke from the valley below... it's gray-blue, rising straight up until it disappears into the clouds.
You speak, sentence by sentence, while she listens with her eyes closed. Her breathing steadies and calms, as if she is on the verge of drifting off to sleep.

steps.speaker: Jichuan
steps.content: Young hero...
...Huh?

steps.speaker: Jichuan
steps.content: The truth is... my illness does have a cure.

steps.speaker: Jichuan
steps.content: The old doctor who took my pulse back then left me a prescription. But the ingredients were too rare... I never could gather them all. Now... I fear it is too late, yet if it is you, there might still be a chance.
She speaks in a rush, as though fearful of running out of time.

steps.speaker: Jichuan
steps.content: Three things are needed: a hundred-year ice lotus core from the snow-capped peaks, which must be plucked before the first light of dawn; crimson flame stone marrow from the depths of southern volcanoes, taken as the lava tide recedes and sealed within a jade box; and also...

steps.speaker: Jichuan
steps.content: Pearls formed from merfolk tears on a night of the full moon in the East Sea, caught while they sing. It must never once touch the earth.

steps.speaker: Jichuan
steps.content: If I could gather them all, this body of mine... might yet linger a while longer in this world.
The shackles clearly relay her true condition: her current vitality is merely the last flicker of warmth before the final fade.
You don't say anything, just watch her quietly. You watch the earnestness she struggles to maintain in those unfocused eyes, and the weakness she can't conceal beneath her pallor.
She mutters quietly, and there is actually a hint of hurt in her voice.

steps.speaker: Jichuan
steps.content: Can you not... pretend to believe me, just this once?
So where exactly do I harvest the ice lotus core? Which ice cave? How long before dawn? Should it be in moonlight or shadow?

steps.speaker: Jichuan
steps.content: The third ice rift on the north side of the main peak, descend a hundred meters to a ledge. It must be gathered between the hours of final darkness and earliest light, when moonlight fades but has not yet surrendered to the sun, and the petals must still be robed in dew—
She stops mid-sentence, her voice trailing into silence. She feels it then: warm droplets landing on the back of her hand, one by one.
A moment later, she musters a smile. It's wan, yet tender.

steps.speaker: Jichuan
steps.content: ...You fool.
She reaches out to wipe the tears from your face, but her hand falls short, her strength giving out.

steps.speaker: Jichuan
steps.content: Never mind. I only ever heard those places were beautiful, and I never had the chance to see them with my own eyes. I thought to trick you into going and looking for me. If you ever pass by there in the days to come, remember to write me a letter... tell me what they look like.
When you get better, we'll go together.
As if her last lingering doubt has finally been put to rest, her whole body goes limp as she settles back against your shoulder.

steps.speaker: Jichuan
steps.content: I'm tired, young hero.
I'll take you back inside.

steps.speaker: Jichuan
steps.content: Not inside... Take me to the window. I wish to see the manor one last time.

Ahead, there is nothing but vast seas of clouds and sheer cliffs, no windows to be found. Her sight has failed her completely. You choose not to correct her, instead guiding her gently toward the light.

steps.speaker: Jichuan
steps.content: ...It's beautiful, is it not? This place where I was born and raised.
Yeah.

steps.speaker: Jichuan
steps.content: The snow upon the eaves... is beginning to melt.
Yeah.

steps.speaker: Jichuan
steps.content: And the plum blossoms in the rear courtyard... they have bloomed fuller than yesterday, have they not?
They have. And the peach trees will bloom soon too.

steps.speaker: Jichuan
steps.content: How wonderful... Spring... has finally come.

Her breathing slows, growing lighter and lighter. You let her rest against you until a faint smile graces her lips, as if she is drifting into a warm dream. Only then do you carry her sleeping form inside, gently covering her with a fur cloak.
The earth is warming, yet her body turns cold. Believing she is only asleep, you tear through the dilapidated manor in search of charcoal.
At the base of the walls, beside the collapsed stove, among the scattered chests... You scour every corner. Clutching two hard-won pieces of charcoal, you finally rush back to the bedside—
The bed is empty now. Only her fur cloak remains, folded into a perfect square. On top of it lie two things:
A withered plum branch and an unsigned letter.
You unfold the letter. The strokes are crooked and wild, the final lines barely legible. The writer has spent her last ounce of strength.
Young hero,

By the time you read this, I fear I will no longer be among the living. Please, do not seek me out. For those who walk the martial world, any green hill can serve as a final resting place. The affairs of the manor have been entrusted to capable hands. The secret codex was never more than an illusion, as greed alone was the true culprit. Within the pages of Chronicles of Northwild on my desk, you will find the full account of the old cases and the brands of those involved. I ask that you make it known.

It was never my wish to deceive you or to make use of your kindness. Circumstances left me no other path. Your sincerity, time and again, broke through the impossible, and for that, I am both deeply shamed and profoundly moved. Our first meeting at the inn, the journey together through the snowy night, the peril we faced in the pine woods, the ascent up the cliff... all these became unexpected light in the dwindling days of my life. I am grateful that you were willing to trust me, one last time.
Yet what I have sought all my life was never vengeance, nor the settling of old grudges, nor the purging of corruption. What I sought can be spoken in four simple words: the world serves all.

Those who inherit power in the martial world ought to protect the common people; those born with extraordinary gifts ought to aid all living beings. This truth is simple, and yet it has been forgotten. I offer my body as kindling, to burn through this wind and snow, not to illuminate my own name, but in the hope that this flame may light the way for those who follow.

Young hero, I know you came seeking the truth of the secret codex. That scroll of blank paper was scattered somewhere during the final battle. I would counsel you to search for it no longer. Though you are not of Northwild, you were willing to draw your sword against injustice. A heart and will such as yours far surpass any divine martial art.

P.S.: If you ever pass by the old wall at the west market below the mountain, would you feed the wild sparrows that gather there for me? Among them, there may be two particularly unruly ones who always quarrel over food. I saved them during my days wandering the martial world as Shuang'er.
Jichuan
P.S.: The plum branch is yours. My mother once said that daughters should be like plum flowers, blooming fragrant even in frost. In my life... do you think I managed to become such a bloom?
At the end of the letter, there is a spot where the ink has blurred from moisture; it is still warm to the touch.

You hold the letter, standing in the empty chamber. Morning light fills the room. In the courtyard, the mist has completely cleared, and above the manor, the vast sky stretches, azure and crystal clear.
[Manor Gate]
Xiaofeng props herself against the stone lion, a grass stem tucked in the corner of her mouth. Spying you, she lifts a single, questioning eyebrow.

steps.speaker: Xiaofeng
steps.content: Off so soon?

Yeah. Should've left the first time I came down the mountain. Staying this long is already pushing it. Just wish I had more time. I finally got to Eastia, and there are old friends I won't get to see.
Xiaofeng tosses you a coarse cloth bundle. You catch it and find dried rations, a water pouch, and a hand-drawn crude map inside.

steps.speaker: Xiaofeng
steps.content: The path down the mountain is clear. Meowy saw to that. Horse at the post station, fresh and sturdy. Call it a thank-you for letting me watch this grand show.
The show's over. Where to now?

steps.speaker: Xiaofeng
steps.content: Me? Back to my den on White Tiger Mountain. Gonna loaf around till Eastia kicks up another fuss. Then I'll wander out again.
So you came all the way up the mountain with me just for the fun of it?

steps.speaker: Xiaofeng
steps.content: ...Hard to say. Watching you walk off through the snow, getting smaller... reminded me of this dream I keep having.

steps.speaker: Xiaofeng
steps.content: Bunch of scrawny kids huddled up in the mountain lord temple, kowtowing to my dusty old statue, crying, "Please, Mountain Lord, open your eyes and help us..." Didn't want you showing up in my dreams too, so, here I am.
You nod. Before leaving, you give Meowy a scratch under the chin.
Probably sounds strange, but I've got a feeling we'll meet again. Not in a dream, though.

steps.speaker: Xiaofeng
steps.content: Sure, sure. Now go. Keep yapping and it'll be dark again.
She turns and walks toward the deep forest, waving at you over her shoulder without looking back.

steps.speaker: Xiaofeng
steps.content: Hang onto that wooden branch the beggar girl gave you. It's gonna come in handy.
[Inn]
And sure enough, outside the mid-mountain inn, a chestnut stallion stands tethered to a post, its hooves pawing the ground with impatience.

You have no idea how to ride, but you attempt to mount it anyway. The horse snorts loudly and spins twice, nearly bucking you off. Luckily, it catches the scent of the tiger on you and quickly resigns itself to its fate, plodding along as it carries you down the mountain.
Wind whistles past your ears. Snowy pines blur on either side. The winding road descends, and the view gradually opens up. You see—

Streams flow again with the melting snow, their babbling crisp and bright. On sun-facing slopes, patches of grass appear in mottled hues, tender green scattered through the withered yellow. Where wild plum blossoms have fallen by the roadside, tiny buds swell on the branches.
As you pass through the small town at the mountain's base, you slow your horse to a gentler pace. Children chase one another along the street when one suddenly points at you and calls out.

steps.speaker: Child A
steps.content: Hero! Look, look, the Cold Egg Palms I just learned! Hi-yah! Ha!
Several unfamiliar children gather around, their upturned faces bright, each one with the same sparkling eyes as Shuang'er.

steps.speaker: Child B
steps.content: Mister, did you come from the mountain? Did you see Shuang'er?
steps.female_content: Miss, did you come from the mountain? Did you see Shuang'er?

steps.speaker: Child A
steps.content: Shuang'er said she'd tell us stories about the manor, but she probably forgot again, took her little ratty bag, and went off adventuring. Soon as I'm good enough, I'm gonna chase her down and drag her back!
You gently pat their grubby but hope-filled faces.
You're not wrong. Shuang'er took that ratty old bag, left us all behind, and went off to live free as a bird.

She said she was heading to a place far, far away, a place where martial arts masters go to retire. Sages in the mist, smiling as they take in students, teaching a few moves, then drinking under the moon and swapping stories from the martial world.
The children don't quite understand, but a chorus of "Wow!" erupts from them.

You press your horse forward through a countryside dotted with villages, each one sending up peaceful wisps of cooking smoke. Beneath the eaves, the elderly sit soaking in the sun, their eyes half-closed in a state of quiet contentment.

steps.speaker: Old Woman
steps.content: Good weather we're having. Good for planting.
A soft, warm breeze moves through the wasteland. It's a sensation you never appreciate back in the DisCity, where the air offers no such comfort.
You think what Jichuan did... could it really affect the calamities here?

steps.speaker: Schorl
steps.content: Theoretically, it's unlikely. For a collective will to meaningfully alter calamities, it typically requires ritual frameworks or mediums, similar to Seer practices, to serve as a conduit.

Maybe the conduit was already there? Myths are conduits. Martial arts legends are conduits. Stories, lies... they're like sunlight, like air, anything that gives people hope when they've got nothing left. Maybe that's enough.
You hear the inn server as he slaps down his tea bowl.

steps.speaker: Attendant
steps.content: "Let me tell you the legend of Jichuan, Master of Northsnow Manor, a soul daring enough to dream of mending the world! Witnessing the rot festering within the martial world and tasting the bitter tears of the common folk, she wove herself into the bait, a gleaming lure for the wolves of wickedness. With spirit unbroken and arts divine, she swept through Northwild, purging its tainted breath until, at last, the snows relented and spring, long-exiled, returned to the land of men—"

steps.speaker: Schorl
steps.content: This is the story you had me transmit to DisCity for Yugu to refine.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: This is a story of Eastia's Northwild. Let it stay here. We won't be back for a long time.
The story has begun to spread. Through word of mouth, truth and legend interweave, taking on vibrant new life.

Soon, new children will sit at street corners, raised on these tales, and seeds of heroism will be planted alongside them. Perhaps one day, some among them truly become Sinners who shield their land through acts of benevolence, or even... new Seers.
The flame of heroism burns eternal, and the martial world endures forever.
[Grassland]

You finally learn to control your horse, gently squeezing its flanks as the steed breaks into a full gallop toward the brightening dawn. Wind billows your robes, and the letter tucked against your chest rustles with each stride.
Something suddenly comes to mind, and you turn back to look in the direction of Northsnow Manor—

The manor's ruins stand quietly on the mountain peak, bathed in golden light. And in a corner where no one pays attention, that scroll, once the spark for countless greedy conflicts, hangs unrolled from the branches of the plum tree on the cliff's edge.
Mountain wind brushes past, causing the scroll to sway gently. Its surface is completely blank, revealing no martial techniques, no secrets.
Only at the very end, a line of childish, crooked handwriting appears. As if, many years ago, two children huddled at a candy shop entrance, scribbled down a promise with a charcoal pencil.
"Pinky promise, cross my heart, hope to die if I ever lie—"
"You'll be an amazing manor master, and I'll be an amazing hero!"
"We'll ride across the world together, swords in hand, to the very ends of the earth!"
Beside the words, in the blank space of the paper, a crudely sketched little bird sits near a small flower with five petals, forever frozen in time.
[Horseback Riding CG]
